recipes.name: Sesame Pasta Chicken Salad
ingredients_raw: 3 cups shredded, cooked chicken breast meat

steps.text: Heat a skillet over medium-high heat. Add sesame seeds, and cook stirring frequently until lightly toasted. Remove from heat, and set aside.
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add pasta, and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, or until al dente. Drain pasta, and rinse under cold water until cool. Transfer to a large bowl.
In a jar with a tight-fitting lid, combine vegetable oil, soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, sugar, sesame seeds, ginger, and pepper. Shake well.
Pour sesame dressing over pasta, and toss to coat evenly. Gently mix in chicken, cilantro, and green onions.

raw_recipe.headline: Sesame Pasta Chicken Salad
raw_recipe.description: A refreshing light pasta salad with a delicious Asian flair. Great for a summer cookout or picnic.

video.description: In this video, we make a pasta salad shine with a flavorful sesame seed dressing. The dressing has soy sauce, rice vinegar and ground ginger. And the best part? You make it directly in a jar. Add cooked chicken and your favorite vegetables, and the salad is ready.

review.reviewBody: This is my favorite recipe that I have found at allrecipes.com - I fell in love with it when I was making (and tasting) the sauce! The sauce is AMAZING and so delicious, really to die for, and it *makes* the dish. The sauce is the perfect combination of sweet and salty, aromatic and delightful. I make this in huge batches and I add cherry tomatoes, blanched snap peas, baby carrots, and celery. We eat it as the main course, and we have yummy leftovers for the day after. I have made this recipe over and over again.

I've received many compliments on this recipe, having served it a few times. I would only alter a few things: add julienned carrots, sliced water chestnuts and pea pods cut in half on an angle- really adds nice color, texture and flavor. Knock oil down to 1/3 cup otherwise it is REALLY oily. I use fettucine noddles. If you are making this ahead and chilling it (which I would recommend), add half of the dressing while noodles are still warm and will soak up flavor. MMM! Toss the other half of the dressing before serving. I like it warm OR cold, but feel it is better cold. Still great the next day. Will make again and again!!

To DIE for! I reduced the oil to 1/3 cup to make it lower in fat, added a cup of frozen cooked peas and 2 chopped Roma tomatoes for some veggies. Since I love cilantro so much, I increased it to 1/2 cup. The dressing was just amazing! Thanks so much for the recipe!

I had some cooked chicken and cilantro to use so tried this. We had it tonight and ate it warm. Super easy and quick to throw together and yummy. I used linguine and added shredded carrots, pea pods and chopped red pepper. Made the rest as described in recipe. It kind of tasted like Phad Thai. I like sesame taste and thought this was too mild in that regard, however, i want to see what it tastes like tomorrow after cooled and had a chance to settle overnight. Would be great topped with chopped peanuts or cashews!! Hubby loved it and had 3 helpings!! Great for a summer meal. I will definitely make this again. Thanks for the recipe. Update: Had it cold tonight....even better!! Son ate 2 helpings saying delicious, delicious. You could taste the sesame a bit more but I am going to increase the sesame oil next time. UPDATE: I have made this many times. I usually make it as a cold pasta salad without chicken. I typically use farfalle or rotini as it is easier to eat. I tweaked it a bit to my liking. II decrease the oil to 1/3 cup and I add 2 tsp of the sesame oil. I also usually add chopped red pepper, chopped pea pods and shredded carrots in addition to the other vegetables in the recipe. I pour the dressing on while the pasta is warm, let it cool and refrigerate over night. I add the chopped vegetables the next day. It is delicious and well liked by family!

My family loved this recipe! I followed some reviewers suggestions and added a half a bag of diagonally sliced snow peas and two thirds cup shredded carrots during the last minute of the pasta boil time, drained it all together, and added half the dressing while the pasta was still slightly warm, adding the remaining dressing with the rest of the ingredients. I also reduced the vegetable oil to 1/4 cup and increased the sesame oil to 2 tablespoons. I added extra green onions for crunch and flavor and topped with the juice of half a lime. Lastly, for extra flavor, we pre-marinated the chicken in a bottled Island teriyaki sauce and grilled it before we cooled and chopped it and added it to the salad. Delicious dish!

I have been making a variation of this recipe for nearly 20 years. It is a nice, light and refreshing dish to serve at BBQs or potlucks. I always make it as a meatless side dish. 

I find that any shaped pasta is fine for this recipe. It doesn't really matter. I also have been adding diced green and red peppers, shredded and diced carrots, and peas (frozen or canned with no salt) for color and texture.

This recipe is best when made at least 4-6 hours in advance. I like to make it 24 hours in advance. It stores very nicely in the refrigerator. Just keep it sealed in a glass or plastic dish with lid. The day you are serving, just shake really well to combine ingredients.

I reduced the vegetable oil to 1/4 cup, and added some chopped carrots and red bell pepper. I also just diced up the chicken and sautéd in a pan instead of shredding. Super easy and great to pack for lunches for the week!

Loved it!! I did it in the crock pot because it's super good to have in the summer and I don't want to stand over a hot stove for a long period of time. I used a plastic bag crock pot liner and threw in everything except the noodles. I also reduced the olive oil to about 1/3 C. Cooked in the crock pot for about 5-6 hours on low, then shredded the chicken, put it back in the bag, and stuck the whole bag in the fridge until it was cool. I boiled noodles on the stove, then rinsed them under cold water and added them to the bag as well for about 1/2 hour for the flavors to come together. Everyone loved it.

Love love love the dressing. I doubled everything in the dressing except the oil and sugar. (Used 1/2 the oil and 3/4 sugar called for). I had a lot of chicken and added extra vegetables so I wanted plenty. The flavor combinations are spot on for a great salad. In addition to what was called for, I added a couple shredded carrots and a bag of shelled edamame. Can’t wait to try it with cucumbers this summer. Broccoli or maybe some shredded cabbage would be good too. This is a keeper. Thanks for the recipe.

This is a huge hit for a "team meal"! Made many times for different groups, and everyone raved. 
I cut back the oil a bit. I use only about 2/3 of the dressing, so I reserve the toasted sesame seeds and toss them in later. (Since I want all of them in the salad). 
To cook the chicken breasts: Bring water to a boil ( I add in some teriaki if I have it) add chicken breasts with water to cover 1/2 inch over. Return to boil, cover, remove from heat and let sit 15-20 minutes.

Very good summer dish. I completely ignored the proportions for the dressing and made it to taste, leaving out the vegetable oil. Likewise, I made it vegetarian with eggplant, bell peppers and zucchini, but could work with so many more veggies. I also lightly sautéed the veggies in sesame oil, ginger and hot pepper seeds. Then cooled and added the cilantro, dressing and sesame seeds. Next time will do with cashews. Enjoy!
Not enough sesame oil, and I used fresh ginger and garlic.
I haven't tried this yet, but as a rule, I love sesame noodles. I'm going to try this. But without the chicken and adding some vegetables. And maybe a little chili crisp.

I tried to follow the recipe as written, but my cupboard wasn't as well stocked as I thought. I only had about half of the amount of Rice Wine Vinegar called for. So I used Cider Vinegar for the other half. I had a jar of toasted sesame seeds so didn't need to do step one. I served the salad at room temperature after it had aged for about an hour. I also cheated by buying a rotisserie (spelling) chicken and shredding that meat. I think this salad is excellent! The cider vinegar may have added a taste that you wouldn't have with the plain rice wine vinegar...and next time I'll be sure to have enough of that on hand. Thank you for this recipe!
This is one of my favorite dishes! It is easy to put together, delicious, and it can be made healthier if you want by adding vegetables. The sauce makes it especially good.

I used some odds and ends of noodles I had and used less oil and sugar as others had suggested. I had some left over rotisserie chicken and added celery and grated carrots. So delicious! I’ll be making this all summer!
Definitely allow it to marinate in fridge overnight. Very good and the 2nd day I added a drizzle of mirin and thai sweet chili to one serving and that was good too.

For starters, I used fusilloni pasta, chopped rotisserie chicken, and added 1/3 cup of matchstick carrots. The carrots were added for a bit of color. The dressing was made exactly as written. Cilantro, green onion, and sesame seeds were the amounts stated. This was not too sweet nor too oily. I almost added an additional 1-2 tsp of sugar but, didn't because I wanted to stick to the recipe. It is in the refrigerator now. When you taste it freshly made you just know the flavor will be better cold. Next time, I will use whole wheat pasta, 2/3 cup carrots and 4-5 tsp of Swerve to make it a little healthier. Overall, a very good recipe. I'm editing my review. I tasted this freshly made, after refrigeration, and microwaved after it was cold. Tried it with Sriracha, tried it with soy sauce. I have to change my rating to 3.9. This just didn't turn out as expected. I might try again but, I'd focus on other reviewer suggestions. There are other better pasta salads.
I reduced the oil and sugar by half and added peas, carrots and cashews. I think this would also be delicious with any variety of vegetables. Water chestnuts would be be excellent as well.
